text: I play OOTP every day, but I cannot recommend this game any longer. Don't let the fact that I have tons of hours mislead you... it’s more a reflection of habit and addiction. If I didn’t get the game for free as part of the beta team, I honestly wouldn’t be buying it. Perfect Team is a financial success, but creatively, it’s the biggest misstep the franchise has made. It shifted focus and resources away from the core game. After all these years, can anyone really say the offline experience has improved dramatically? Many longtime players would argue it has regressed. I could write a 10,000-word essay on all of its issues, but here are some highlights in no particular order: - OOTP is poorly optimized for 2025. A single save file can balloon into hundreds of thousands of files, creating a massive burden for backups, syncing, and long-term storage. In short, cloud saves are just not feasible. - The in-game 3D remains frustrating. Animations are rough, results aren’t physics-based, and the follow-ball feature is disorienting. After more than a decade of development, I still stick with 2D because 3D is just not good. - Game mechanics are bloated and inaccessible. Concepts like traditional player creation modifiers, sabermetric modifiers, league totals, and league total modifiers are scattered and unintuitive, especially for new users. - Online leagues are outdated. There’s no official server support, so commissioners must know how to set up their own server or pay someone to do it. More importantly, there are no anti-cheat tools. Commissioners can view or edit ratings, and concerns about this are often brushed off. A simple player editor lock would go a long way to improve online league transparency and integrity. - Documentation and support remain major weaknesses. Bug reports frequently go unanswered, and there’s no official manual to help players understand how the game’s many systems interact. It’s trial and error, even for veterans. - The community wiki helps, but it’s often outdated or too vague. Developers have been hesitant to explain how core mechanics actually function, citing a desire to preserve mystery. In practice, this just makes the game harder to understand and harder to teach. - The game often feels unpolished at launch. While there is some internal testing, the bulk of beta testing is handled by unpaid volunteers like myself, most of whom have full-time jobs and other commitments. As a result, the testing window before release is inconsistent, and many issues simply don’t surface until after launch. Despite everything, I keep coming back to OOTP because no other game offers this level of control over a baseball organization. The depth of strategy, both on the field and in roster building, is still unmatched. Even when the mechanics frustrate and confuse me, the foundation of the game is strong enough to keep me engaged. Customization is another huge draw. Whether I want to replay a historical season, build a completely fictional universe, or run a modern league with my own twist, OOTP gives me the tools to do it. Few games offer this kind of creative freedom. I’ve also built a lot of familiarity with the game over the years. I know how to work around most of its limitations, and at this point, it feels more like a sandbox than a traditional game. Most importantly, running an online league is still fun. The stories, rivalries, and personalities that emerge from human interaction are what bring OOTP to life. The software might frustrate me, but the online league experience is what keeps me coming back.

You can feel the Com2us in this version. And that's not a good thing. All the effort is in Perfect Team, their cash grab slot machine. The base game is the same as ever with a few additions like the development lab, which, while fun in theory, break the entire idea of player development as handled by the organization (including setting a budget for). I would have liked to have seen maybe more detail put into the lab like having your highest ranked prospects get more time with coaches or the such as they might in real life. Pros: * Simulation aspect still seems up to snuff * Controlling a team over several years is still a fun exercise in balancing budgets with talent * Game play remains relatively unchanged from previous solid versions Cons: * Too much emphasis and dev time spent on Perfect Team and it shows * Rosters for 2025 are constantly incorrect, even in live start sometimes * Schedules for 2025 are incorrect * Still no way to copy league settings between saves thus requiring 15min+ to set up each new save file * AI minor league managers now DFA prospects if you're not watching * Minor league DFA's show up under MLB DFA screen making it needlessly busy * Mail/News now includes many things not relevant to your team or organization and even changing the filter still keeps the notifications in place making you check all the time anyway * Inclusion of additional in-game currencies for Perfect Team * Accounting and team budgets are still broken requiring constant editor changes to owner finances to make things make sense (even just for the 2025 season). And the consequences of being over budget are still ridiculous (who would actually gut their scouting department budget for the overall team being $1 over budget with a Win Now owner?) Example, the Dodgers, lavish spenders that they are, start the game "over budget," without a 6 man rotation, a gutted scouting budget, and if not on the Live Start, they mysteriously have Anthony Rendon on the IL (obviously put on the wrong LA team). This also makes the AI make stupid trade moves to get back under budget. Suggestion is if you have 23 or 24 and you don't mind not having the latest rosters, keep playing those and skip 26. If you, like me, need the latest rosters then wait for 26 to go on sale and pick it up. The original devs apparently no longer work on OOTP and you can feel the difference in the focus.

I'll be honest - I'm part of the problem. I buy Madden pretty much every year (or every other year), fully aware that it barely ever changes. And usually? I still get some enjoyment out of it. It's always been a decent game to just jump into for a few chilled games of football, especially in Franchise or Superstar mode. But Madden 26 has genuinely pushed that patience to its limit. The biggest issue is stability. The game CONSTANTLY freezes, and the EA servers are an absolute mess. Disconnects happen way too often, to the point where finishing a full game in Superstar mode fells like a coin toss. There's nothing worse than investing time into a match or your career, only for it to crash or boot you out for no reason. And then there's multiplayer... which could be fun, but just isn't. It's completely overrun with microtransactions. If you dare go online, you're almost guaranteed to come up against someone with a ridiculously stacked team that you simply can't compete with unless you're willing to spend extra money. It feels heavily pay-to-win, which just kills any motivation to even try. What's frustrating is that I want to enjoy this game. The core idea is still there, and I've always liked the career modes. But between the technical issues and the monetisation, it's just not worth the hassle this time around. Easily one of the worst Maddens in recent years - and that's saying something.

I've returned to Out of the Park after about 15 years. The long and the short of it is that this appears to continue to be the best baseball sim on the market. If you want to play this type of game, you pay the cost of admission. For the most part you should be greatly satisfied. However, there are numerous frustrations that while not game-breaking or experience-ruining, they'll significantly sully the experience. [Edit: Even though I highly recommend this game warts and all, I've selected "No" to call out its numerous issues.] While there's certainly a lot that's been added to the series since I played it, there's also a lot that really hasn't changed or improved much. Obviously I have no trouble paying to upgrade from the last version I purchased many years ago, but I would anticipate being frustrated to upgrade year after year. Most of the issues are interface-based. Broadly, the interface is great! It's functional, and to an extent customizable. However it does not play well with certain resolutions, and some screens/areas are just trash. A few examples: The pending free agent offers screen can't be sorted which makes it an absolutely nightmare if you're negotiating with large groups of players at once. On the depth chart screens, removing a player from the lineup also pulls them out of the depth chart. And adding a player to the depth chart as a starter automatically puts them in the first empty lineup spot. Why?? This is a nuisance when I want to build and reorganize them individually. As well, you have to be super-accurate when dragging and dropping on this screen as well as the scouting one, or else the item you've selected just disappears. Drop-down menus just aren't well organized. There are so, so many screens and reports. On one hand that's marvellous! But it takes forever to find and memorize the location of what you're looking for. Many links are duplications. Why does the Combine Scouting shortcut just take you to a partially-functioning Team Home Screen if that function is disabled? My BIGGEST GRIPE is that the game STILL lacks proper documentation. I remember the game lacking a manual way back in the day, or it would come out long after the yearly game release. These days, a manual doesn't exist. I member of the community told me documentation is now wiki-based. Well, yes, a wiki exists. But it's incomplete and some entries are outdated. As well, it appears to be maintained by the community rather than the development team. A lot of the information seems to be cobbled together from developer posts on the official forums. (But I'm not 100% certain of this.) The community is fractured between the offical forums, the subreddit, and the Discord server, as well as the few mods on Steam Workshop. Having all these avenues of contact isn't a bad thing! And I'm relieved the forum still exists, many companies opt for insufficient Discords for troubleshooting and information sharing these days. But it means you need to hunt between all of them to find what you're looking for. The best way to research a particular topic is the plug it into a search engine with "Reddit" appended to the query. But the issue here is that a lot of available information is for previous versions of the game, and while often it's still applicable, other times it's not. The official Discord is fairly busy and well populated, and the community has provided helpful answers to some of my questions. But others have gone unanswered. If there was adequate documentation for the game, I wouldn't have had to ask! And I'm not talking about asking how the under-the-hood, "fog of war"-style engine components function. I don't expect that stuff to be revealed, not in specific detail anyway. Many of those features can be disabled if you don't want to bother with them. I'm referring to core functions of the game that should be clearly explained. I made a detailed bug report on the forum that was completely ignored. On multiple occasions I submitted an offer to a free agent that exceeded their demand. They replied by declining my offer and requesting a lesser amount! Ridiculous. I also reported it on the Discord and a community member just replied to the effect of "Yeah, contract negotiations have multiple issues. It really needs to be looked at in the next version." What a brainwashed sentiment. Online leagues remain one of the best ways to experience the game in my opinion, but they're even more complex and drawn out than they used to be due to all the features that have been added on over the years. Of course, the commissioner/league admin can choose to disable many of these systems. But even a basic online league requires an extremely dedicated and knowledgeable commissioner. I find the much-maligned Perfect Team card-collecting mode to be a hollow experience. I had a lot of fun with it for a couple of weeks, and you can definitely accomplish a lot as a player who doesn't buy extra packs through pay currency. But this is mainly facilitated by farming the daily Twitch drops, five each from official and community streams. This requires three total hours of having Twitch open in your browser. Of course, you can mute the tab and don't have to actively watch or have it open in the foreground. But it feels like work. Another way to get ahead is by completing collection missions, which is just what it sounds like. Acquire the listed cards from packs or by buying them with in-game currency on the in-game auction house, which just unlocks more cards and packs. This will allow you to dominate the early leagues. However, it also means once you get to a certain level, almost everyone will be running the exact same cards. It's boring. Listing cards on the action house is also a chore, and the interface is maddening in that you get a pop-up whenever you sell a card, interrupting whatever you're doing and sometimes resetting your menu action. Infuriating! I also seem to get logged out of Perfect Team mode at least once per day, and there's no option for the password entry field not to hide your typed characters. Why?? Who's playing OOTP in a public place where passers-by are going to steal their Perfect Team login information? It's absurd. As well, while the Perfect Team leagues pit you against other players, there's absolutely no social interaction in-game. Some players list their forum or Discord handles in their profiles, so I guess you could look them up there or just chat in the general Discord channels for this mode. The draft-based tournaments are also interesting if you like draft-based CCG-style modes--many are free to enter, and you don't have to have the cards in your collection. But I tried it for a bit and I really don't see the depth. Since the simulated games add a lot of randomness (I mean, it's what the simulation engine does), it all feels like a crapshoot. A lot of people seem really into the Perfect Team mode--there's certainly a lot to do. Another component is the daily fantasy-baseball-like mode that allows you to guess the day's real-world top performers (as long as you own their cards). But after a while that too grows boring. Anyway, I'm glad this mode provides an additional revenue stream for the developers. But it really does make it feel like aspects of the main game are neglected. A lot just doesn't seem to change from version to version, and there are multiple features that are in dire need of an overhaul. Despite all this, the core of the game is largely excellent and as deep and engaging as ever. You can get lost here for hundreds if not thousands of hours. I still recommend the game. I just wish it seemed like the developers even cared about these issues. Note: My playing time is misleading, as I leave the client open all day when I'm monitoring my Perfect Team league or intermittently working on my online player league rosters. But I've still invested beyond 100 hours as of the writing of this review.

I was hoping for a realistic football management experience, but it honestly feels more like an Excel simulator than a game. The interface is extremely dated, the menus are clunky, and the entire experience feels like something from 15-20 years ago. It doesn’t feel intuitive or engaging. There’s no presentation or immersion. You get text, stats, and endless clicking through confusing menus. It’s hard to get a real sense of building or managing a team when everything feels so flat and lifeless. I was also hoping for some kind of feedback from coaches or staff. Anything to make it feel like your decisions matter. Instead, you get what comes from the news section, and even that’s sparse and repetitive. The one thing that this game had going for it were the NFL rosters. You have to navigate the dusty corners of the internet to get everything else (logos and team names) though. The concept has potential, but the execution is rough. For the price, I expected something more polished, modern, and user-friendly. As it stands, Front Office Football 9 feels like what it is; a spreadsheet disguised as a football sim.

TLDR: It's EA, costs way too much for the quality of the game, franchise is decent, Superstar is godawful, the rest of the game is fine, bugs are plentiful, but I still have fun playing. Look, it's a madden game. It costs way too freaking much for what you're getting. If you buy them every year your gonna do the same this year. BUT, if you're actually on the fence, here's the breakdown: Franchise mode is actually kinda fun. New coaching abilities are harder to understand and seemingly do even less than previous years, but the rest of the mode is decent. They removed a lot of the annoying filler things like the end of year interviews about promising position upgrades and what not. Scouting, drafts, and free agency are fun for me, and I enjoy gearing up for a new season. Playing the seasons are fun too. Good players demand way too much money on their contract years which can be infuriating, but otherwise, the money management with salary cap can be fun. Overall, franchise is a 7/10 this year for me. Superstar mode sucks so bad its actually embarrassing. Compared to CFB 26's road to glory, its buggier, less fleshed out, way less climactic, and a waste of time. Roster spots are based on coach trust, not your overall rating. There aren't position battles, so getting the #1 position spot is a boring endeavor. Getting weekly awards or MVP is honestly really stupidly anticlimactic, and winning the super bowl as a rookie (which is stupidly easy to do by the way) gets you literally nothing special. The whole game mode sucks this year, and they have to do better next year. Online/Quick Play is always serviceable, so nothing to report on there. Bugs are plentiful as always. Whether you catch the ball out of bounds and it gives you the first down anyway, or it gives you a stat in franchise mode telling you the numbers but not the actual stat, or buggy camera things, or not doing the play you picked, or a million other things, there are way too many bugs. Will they fix them? Almost definitely not. It'll be what it'll be. That all said, I mostly have fun playing this game. So I'll give it either a 3/10 or a 6/10 depending on the gamemode I play and how buggy the madden gods decide to make my game.

OOTP 26 has completely ruined franchise mode with its extreme over-normalization of player abilities. Star players no longer feel special — everyone is just marginally better or worse than everyone else. This kills the excitement of acquiring talent and makes managing a team feel pointless and unengaging. Perfect Team mode is somewhat entertaining at first, but it quickly hits a wall once whales dominate the market, making it nearly impossible to compete without spending real money. You might enjoy the game in short bursts, but I would not recommend buying it at full price.

I have been a lifelong madden fan on console. Now that I have a computer, I was excited to try it here. The graphics are better, I can use whatever controller I want. Unfortunately, this game just is not fun. Especially since I've tried NBA 2K26 and seen what a sports game can really be like. For the past few weeks, I've been trying franchise mode and superstar (the career mode) and it just hasn't been fun. The madden gameplay feels broken at times. Players bug out. Wide receivers drop the ball far too often following a catch. Playing with a mediocre quarterback means that some passes just go straight into the defender's hands. Nothing you can do about it. The career mode is a time waste. Period. There is so much needless and boring filler to try to create these "story moments" that it makes the mode feel slow. Every week you are presented with some kind of "choice" like this: A meme has gone viral of you falling down. Your agent wants to take it down and your hacker (yes, you are friends with a hacker I guess?) is offering to do it. However, fans will think you're being a bad sport if you do." Choosing either one has no real ramification and just takes an extra 2 minutes of time. And you do it every week. Madden is a middling game now made only buyable because of an exclusive agreement between EA and the NFL and it's ruined the game for me. Sad. 2/10
Overall the game lacks way too much. No legend rosters, poor franchise mode, play now is lackluster. Copy and past every year.

However, I wanted to rebuild the Jets, shopped around Kyle Connor, every trade offer was a 1 star player and a late round pick, immediately closed the game and requested a refund. If trades are broken in a sports management game there really isnt a point in playing it.

Two years of waiting. FM25 cancelled. “Biggest leap in series history.” New Unity engine. In/out of possession tactics. Women’s football. The hype was nuclear. What we got is the football management equivalent of turning up to a Champions League final and finding the pitch is a muddy school field with a goalpost missing and the ref is a guy who keeps freezing mid whistle. The UI is a crime. They took the perfectly functional FM24 menus, ran them through a blender, then redesigned them for a tablet owned by someone who’s never played FM. Everything that used to take one click now takes four. Information is buried like they were embarrassed of it. Half the buttons feel like they were designed by someone who hates FM. Navigating this thing is more stressful than actually managing a relegation scrap. Bugs? We got bugs. Freezing mid match. Soft locks. Misaligned text. Buttons that just… don’t work. Players doing things that would get them sectioned in real life. The match engine looks better (credit where it’s due), but the rest of the game feels like it was assembled by interns who were told “just ship it, the contractual obligations are due.” Missing features at launch, unfinished systems, and the distinct feeling that SI spent the extra year learning Unity by watching YouTube tutorials at 2x speed. Even after months of patches the core problems never went away. Support’s done now. They’re already looking at beta testing FM27 while this one limps along with half the player base still hiding in FM24 like the nuclear bunker its become. I’ve played this series for years. I’ve endured the usual annual quirks. This is the first time I’ve genuinely felt insulted by an FM release. It’s not just “a bit rough around the edges.” It’s a full price beta that somehow still has the audacity to ask for your money and your time. Save yourself. Either stick with FM24 or wait for Sports Interactive to earn your trust back. Or just go outside and touch grass. You'll get more managerial satisfaction watching kids kick a ball in the park. This is the worst one. From development and communication failures, technical and gameplay issues, loss of trust, and I didn't even talk about no International management on a World Cup year.

If EA allowed you to buy past versions of the game there would be no reason to buy this one. The last Madden I bought was '21 and I thought it'd been long enough I get this one. I should've just kept play '21 because this game is a buggy mess of garbage with zero support and no care for the player. There are game breaking bugs and writing scenarios that make no sense and make you wonder who made their 3rd grader do their work for them. I only play Franchise and some Superstar because the multiplayer is only there for microtransactions. Even with just those two modes, which have been in Madden games for many years, I can't go a single gaming session without encountering terrible game design of a bug that wrecks the modicum of enjoyment I occasionally feel when playing this. If it's not the game freezing with 20 seconds left in a half then refusing to present plays to choose from so my players just sit there like idiots for 5 seconds while the clock runs down it's random bugs that spawn the stands on the hashmarks so you can't use half of your throwing options. That's just two of many in-game bugs that ruin immersion and highlight the flaws of this game. In Superstar mode during the playoffs, every week, you'll get the option to practice or play a game of madden against a team mate. If you decide to spend your time at practice the week before a super bowl instead of playing a round of madden your teammate loses favor for you and you get no benefit during the game. If you force a 3-and-out on defense the game says you missed an opportunity, but if your opponent gets a field goal then you did great! If the game sets a goal of getting a B+ or higher and you get an A- minus, guess what, that's not a B+ so you don't get the XP. Every other Madden iteration has it's flaws, but none have ever beaten me over the head with them as much as this one. Don't buy this game no matter how much you like Football. Learn from my mistake.

As a long time player of the game who as been a bit up and down on the state of the game over the past few years, I am very worried about this game's future. What used to be the most accurate sports management simulation game, is now a low performing, bug riddled mess, that strays further from realism every year. The first thing that stands out about this game is just how bad it feels to navigate the menus. The game is slow and unresponsive, and only gets worse the longer your session is. On top of that, I haven't had an OOTP game crash this much since 2015. It is actually astounding how poorly optimized this game is. The ratings and player development overhaul has generally been a very good change for the franchise, but more cracks are showing every year. A great example of this is that the "stuff" rating was flattened out to more closely mimic real life MLB, but pitching potentials were not adjusted, so every pitcher in the game has some unrealized pitching potential that will never be reached. Other than that, the franchise has pretty much gone the way of the console sports games, implementing meaningless changes just to have some new marketing words for each game. The draft combine and Trade deadline timer were a heavy part of the lead up to the release of these games, but pretty much have no actual utility. Another fun thing about OOTP, is the forum to provide feedback to the devs and engage with others who play the game, is rarely operational. It is down for several hours at a time multiple days a week. My last big critique of the game is the increase of the price over time. Years ago, OOTP was a great cheaper alternative to the console sports games, if you cared more about the actual management aspect than actual gameplay. That is no longer true, as the price of OOTP is now up to $50, almost the same price as a Triple A title. If the defining characteristic of the game is supposed to be it's accuracy as a spreadsheet sports management simulator, genuinely what is the point of choosing it over an actual Triple A studio game?

For better or worse, it is OOTP. The trade AI is still terrible, and the improvements over the prior version are very minimal. It's still one of the deepest sports-management experiences available though. The few improvements that the game does have are welcome additions. Was it worth the full price as someone who purchases last years? Probably not. Is it worth it if you have never experienced the game? Yes. I imagine that most people are not new to the series though, and for them I say keep playing OOTP 25.

I should’ve written this review when FM26 first released, but honestly, I completely forgot about the game until now. Having come back to it and thought about what I paid for it, I feel like I should finally say something. I bought Football Manager 26 with a 10% discount at launch, and I still regretted the purchase. To make matters worse, I also spent an additional £7.49 on the in-game editors. For the amount I ended up paying, the game simply wasn't worth it. FM26 feels incomplete, messy, and, in many areas, like it was released before it was ready. There are too many things that feel poorly implemented, unfinished, or like a downgrade from previous entries. Instead of feeling like the next evolution of Football Manager, it often feels like a game still trying to find its footing. I understand that this is a completely new engine for the series and that rebuilding a game as complex as Football Manager takes time. I don't expect everything to be perfect immediately, and I can appreciate that moving to a new foundation will come with problems and growing pains. But that doesn't change the fact that I paid for a finished game, and FM26 doesn't feel like one. At the end of the day, I'm not interested in paying for a game at launch and then waiting years for it to become what I feel it should have been from the beginning. Maybe the series will improve as the developers become more familiar with the new engine and continue building on it. I genuinely hope it does, especially for the people who have stuck with the series. But FM26 has been disappointing enough for me that I've decided this is where I get off. I've been a fan of Football Manager, but after this experience, I no longer have the confidence to keep spending money on future releases in the hope that things will eventually improve. I do not recommend FM26 at any price. If you're genuinely interested in getting into the Football Manager franchise, I would recommend FM24 instead. The club squads and transfers will obviously be outdated, but in my opinion, FM24 is the best Football Manager experience.

There is a lot to like about this game, but all the small things it does wrong add up to the game being unenjoyable and nearly unplayable. - Trading system is awful and is the most egregiously bad thing about FOF9. Teams will have 100% interest and enough draft capital to offer, yet the system doesn't allow it. They will (VERY OFTEN) give away every single available draft pick, resulting in them being awful for years while they recover (assuming they don't trade away those picks too). You are unable to actually create your own trades, you simply select a team and a draft pick/player, then hit the offer button and be given a trade. Its not at all interactable. You can't shop picks and players together, you have to choose one and see what the computer offers. Since it is AWFUL at its job, you are forced to navigate the dreadful trade UI to find a team that will actually put together a trade. It's so horrible. - Parts of the UI are unintuitive and hide important things from the player. It took me about 20 hours to discover where the All-Pro lists were despite looking through resources online. It is also very obtuse to reorder your depth chart and to navigate menus. - Your save files WILL get corrupted. Unless you are actively backing up every single save, corruption is inevitable. I have backed up multiple saves in a row just for each one of them to not work, losing hours worth of progress. You, as a player, should not be responsible for ensuring your save files don't corrupt on every single save. - Less features than FOF8. I haven't played it too much so take this with a grain of salt, but FOF9 lacks a lot of QOL features its previous title had. There are no quick options to change team names and logos as you have to manually edit the game files. There is no option to check what positions you need to draft. - FOF9 focuses too hard on the financial management portion (IMO), resulting which causes the roster management portion of the game to suffer. Players feel more like numbers and statistics than actual players. For example: 1. Occasionally, players will sharply regress and lose their potential. There is no (from what I could discern) explanation as to why this happens and doesn't get brought up at all. It rarely lines up with a major injury or age regression. If you keep them on the roster long enough they may randomly go back up to having potential. 2. Retirement is sudden and has zero warning signs (besides players just being old, at best). Players sometimes randomly retire, even if they are young, with a high overall and no major injury history. 3. Overall rarely truly matters. a 90 overall player can simulate worse than a 40 overall player. 4. Players don't request for trades if they are unhappy, they just have contract holdouts. The game doesn't make it clear if having high loyalty affects contract negotiations. 5. Drafting players in incredibly dull and uninteractive. You can't scout payers individually, you just get an estimate based off the scouting skill of your staff. This means that more often than not you end up simming until your next pick, skimming the estimates without any real thought behind it. 6. There is little feedback on how your players are progressing. The only way to check is by looking directly at their stats. It would be nice to get notified about major improvements or regression from players 7. There isn't a practice squad, so you generally are unable to strategically plan backups. Special teams are also lacking, as it boils down to a simple yes or no "is this player participating in special teams?" 8. While there is a system to show synergy/affinity between some players, it is only on offense and doesn't have a noticeable impact on simulation performance. - The simulation sy stem will sometimes do things that make zero sense. It will start your RB3 even if your RB1 is completely healthy and activated. It will start FBs at WR, NTs and CB, ect. - Players get injured far too often on the default settings. Even lowering them down to half typically results in a starting player getting a major injury every game Overall, I highly recommend you to *NOT* spend 30 bucks on this. There are far better options for American football simulation games. FOF8 is ten dollars cheaper and fully fleshed out if you want a similar game as this. Football Coach: College Dynasty is also 10 dollars cheaper with workshop support, better UI, and more QOL that FOF9 does.

FM26 is by FAR the most disappointing FM title to have ever been released. All core mechanics and concept have either been made worse or completely destroyed, the UI and panels that will be what you spend the most time one are objectively terrible and the upside is nowhere to be seen. An engine change and one extra year in development for what? If you remove every single problem, issue and bug that FM26 has introduced it would still be a disappointing release. Pros: - In/Out of possession is a great idea, a smart and intuitive way to add tactical depth. - The new icons and visuals for teh tactic screen look good and fresh. Cons: Bugs Noticed (For now): - The amazing feature of crashing 1/3 times after a match finishes. IMPORTANT: If you are having this issue make sure whenever you are making tactic changes and especially subs do NOT use the undo button. This has caused most of my crashes. - Players beign dissapointed by not fulfilling pormises that you never made and the lovely fact that the only workaround is by using the paid in-game editor. UI/UX: - UI is terrible and unintuitive, things are placed all over the place, hard to find what you are looking for. - UX is even worse with key panels being 5-7 clicks away. On most panels that it takes you 5- 7 clicks to get there one back button will take you back around 4 clicks for no reason. Panels get stuck all the time during a match and you have to find what panel you need to navigate to and what options you need to press to finally get it unstuck almost as if you are defusing a bomb. - Managing, hiring, firing or doing anything related to stuff has just been made 3 times harder and 2 times less intuitive for no reason at all. - The messages screen has somehow become 10x worse. 9/10 messages you receive will be bloat/slop that is not relevant or useful, you get a lot mroe messages than you used to on previous versions. - Interacting with players or staff is a nightmare. The "Actions" button usually hides about 50 different options withotu any categorization and 99% of said options don't have any visual aid. Most used options (e.g. contracts, trainings/form praise/criticism, individual training) should have a visual cue or icon. - The competitions screen is a mess. Good luck trying to find the competition you are looking for and if you do, good luck finding the information you need. - Finances, even the most basic of information is burried tens of clicks away and navigating to it is a complete guessing game. Note: For a game that is 95% panels/UI I cannot believe what a massacre FM26 has been. It's as if they have no UI/UX Specialist working with them. Training: - Managing training is horrible. You can't copy paste sessions, picking what training you want to do is exactly the same but it was made visually worse and harder to use. You have to change every training one by one unlike previous versions where you could day by day. - Out of possession training never works. - Players are almost always complaining about their individual training. - If you want to change a player's individual training you'll have to first change it to none and THEN after passing some days change it to the different target otherwise they will keep nagging you about how their individual training is not beneficial. - Descriptions from individual training have been removed for some reason. - Individual in/out of possession position training, In possession pos has a list of all standard positions and then all roles for the selected position. Out of possession is split into "Defenders/Midfielders/Attackers" and each category has a dozen different roles. Why are these actions any different at all? Match Preparation/Tactics: - No quick subs. - Trying to swap a player on the combined view doesn't show the visual colors that represent how comfortable they are at said position. - That visual cue exists in the In/Out of possessions view BUT making changes on either will not affect the other so you will have to manually change the players on both views. - Sometimes if you make a change in the In/Out of possession views the player you subbed/swappped will be on a different side. For example you have 2 MCs you make a sub of the MC on the right side In possession, the newly added player will be on the left side when out of possession for some reason. - Quick tactic change uses horizontal arrows "< >" but if you open the detailed view of said tactic the appear vertical and have completely different icons while most don't have any icons at all. There is no consistency between menus that serve the same purpuse. - Some option are hidden behind the detailed view and can't be accessed using the left/right buttons. - When using the "< >" buttons, their hitbox is very small and if you miss it opens up the detailed display that you have to close out of. Match Engine: - Crowd audio will stop after 30 minutes of a match and will only come back if you restart the game only to stop playing again on the next. - Marking is broken. More prominent for player marking tactics that will become zonal out of nowhere for some time before reverting. - The AI is the same old, just as stupid as it's always been, simulation is not more accurate or more realistic. - Visually, player models are hard to distinguish in-match, the ball feels like a bouncy ball, visual clarity is not great especially when it's raining. - Shots hitting the woodwork. From controlled testing of 100 matches I found out an average of 2,84 woodworks against you but an average of 0,19 woodowrks for you. - Corners. When you are the stronger team, you will have most shots on target ending up in a corner and if you watch the highlghts you will see the most unlikely saves/stops you have ever seen. If the match engine decides a shot will end up as a corner don't make it a miracle save every time. - Player condition constantly bugs out going up and down so at a quick glance you have no idea how your team is doing. - Player feelings show only the face now and not the description so you have to hover over them if you want to see details. - Pressing Undo on a sub does undo the change but the In/Out icon still appears and will usually crash the game when the match ends. Youth: - Youth training is hidden away and so hard to find that a lot of people still think it's completely removed. - (Observation)Potential ability for players U18 seems off. Previous versions would get within 1 star. In this one even with 20 ability staff on average they are 2-3 stars off. Since I've only noticed this in youngsters this might be a design choice? Adult players have the regular discrepancy as seen in previous games. Conclusion: My disappointment is immeasurable and my FM experience is ruined. They have done so much damage to the game that they'll probably need to delay the next FM another year just to get on par with FM24 and that's a very sad thing I have to type out. Even if FM26 was a one-time free product it would still be the most disappointing FM version ever released.

Not Recommended — MLS is effectively broken by a known salary-cap bug I bought FM26 specifically in part because I wanted to manage in MLS, and unfortunately the current implementation has a game-breaking issue with salary-cap calculations during contract negotiations. In my FC Cincinnati save, the game correctly shows the club’s actual salary-cap position and available GAM in the roster/registration screens. However, when negotiating a new contract, the Budget Adjustments screen displays obviously incorrect salary-cap figures and fails to recognize the club’s available GAM/TAM. Because those incorrect figures feed into the contract validator, the game can disable “Suggest Terms” and prevent you from signing a player even when the deal should be legal under MLS rules. I was able to reproduce this very clearly with Luca Orellano. The game recognized more than $2 million in available GAM elsewhere, but the contract negotiation screen showed effectively none and would not allow the allocation money to be applied. The result was that a legitimate transfer could not be completed. More concerning, this appears to be a known issue that has already been reported on Sports Interactive’s own bug tracker and has still not been properly resolved. MLS roster rules are complicated, but that makes it even more important that the game’s cap and allocation-money systems work reliably. There is a lot I like about FM26, and I would be happy to change this review if the MLS contract/salary-cap system is fixed. But at the moment I cannot recommend the game to anyone who specifically wants to manage in MLS.

Another year, another full-price update that feels like a bug-riddled beta. As a long-time fan of the franchise, Football Manager 2026 is a massive disappointment. Instead of delivering meaningful innovation, Sports Interactive has released a product hampered by persistent UI glitches, match engine oddities, and long-standing bugs that have gone unaddressed for multiple patch cycles. The main issues: UI Clutter & Overlapping Text: The interface feels messy and poorly tested. Text scaling is broken across several menus, causing data, stats, and squad depth roles to overlap awkwardly—making simple squad navigation frustrating. Match Engine Anomalies: Defending AI remains deeply flawed. Center-backs still freeze or make bizarre positioning decisions during basic opposition through-balls, while wingers continue shooting into the side netting from impossible angles instead of squaring for an easy tap-in. Tactics & Squad Depth Glitches: Changing formations on tactical tiles frequently fails to update across related screens, requiring manual menu-refreshing to display accurate player positioning. Broken Transfer Logic: AI clubs make illogical transfer bids, and mandatory buy-out clauses or loan agreements still trigger bugged upfront payment demands or disappear outright mid-negotiation. Lack of Real Innovation: Beyond minor visual tweaks, the core gameplay loop feels identical to previous titles—except now you're paying full price to quality-test a release that relies on future patches to become playable. Unless SI rolls out a major overhaul patch, save your money and stick to an older, fully patched edition. Verdict: 4/10 — Feels unfinished and unacceptable even after almost a year
